SAP Labs Interview Experience (Internship) 
Sayali Kulkarni | TY EXTC 2020-21 
 
 
Aptitude Test: 
 
The aptitude test was of 60 mins with two sections: 
 
1. MCQs related to DBMS, OOPS, DSA, Web Development. 
 
2. Coding questions: 
 
a. Given an array of dates in the form of strings, it had to be returned in a 
sorted form. This question was pretty straightforward and I was able to 
solve it using a custom comparator. I was able to pass all the test cases. 
Refer this → https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sort-an-array-of-string-of-
dates-in-ascending-order/ 
 
b. Three objects were given, namely Circle, Rectangle and Square. Classes 
had to be created for each object, and given the parameters for finding 
area for each object, area had to be returned for each object. This 
question was solved in no time since it was very easy. I was able to pass 
all the test cases. 
 
Only 20 people out of almost 200 were selected for the Interview.  
 
 
Interview Round 1 – (Technical)  
 
The interview took place on CodePair and lasted for almost 30 mins. The 
interviewer was strict and less talkative, so I had to make sure that the discussion 
goes on. I was asked to introduce myself followed by a series of questions on 
OOPS, DBMS, C++, DSA. 
 
1. What is object-oriented programming? Difference between procedural 
programming and object-oriented programming.  
2. Exception handling in C++. Explain in detail the working of try, catch and 
throw expressions.  
3. She tried to ask me some questions related to python but I was not sure 
about it, so I told her that I am not confident about Python.  
4. What types of sorting algorithms do you know? I said Bubble sort, Selection 
sort, Merge sort, Quick sort, Counting sort, Radix sort, etc. She asked me to

explain each algorithm in short with time complexity, stability, space 
complexity, whether it is in place sorting or not, etc.  
5. Interfaces in Java. Interfaces vs Abstract classes 
6. What are virtual functions? 
7. What is Polymorphism? What is function overloading?  
8. Function overloading vs Function overriding 
9. What is linked list? Types of linked lists. Applications of every type of 
linked list.  
10. What is RDBMS? Advantages and disadvantages.  
11. What is a thread in Java? What is multithreading?  
12. ACID properties.  
13. What is index? Types of indexes. Advantages of Clustered over Non-
clustered index.  
 
I was able to answer almost all the questions.  
 
She also asked to write a code again for sorting the dates (I was really surprised 
because same question was there in the aptitude test too). I explained her 
everything line by line while writing the code. I was asked to run the code too, and 
thankfully all the test cases passed! 
 
I was also asked to write a DBMS query. There is a table of containing attributes 
employee id and salary. I was asked to return the third largest salary. But the catch 
was that I was not allowed to use any keyword like LIMIT or SORT BY. I had to 
do it using only greater than and less than operator. I was able to find the largest 
salary in the table, and told the interviewer that I will have to use nested queries. 
She said I am on the right track, but in the end, I was not able to solve it.  
 
Apart from this, she touched every part of my resume. Then, she finally asked if I 
had a question for her. I asked her about the virtual onboarding in case the 
internship programme needs to be conducted online due to the pandemic.  
 
Just after 15 mins, I was invited for the round 2. Almost 8 people were selected for 
round 2.   
 
 
Interview Round 2 – (Technical)  
 
This interview took place on Microsoft Teams. It lasted for almost 30 mins. The 
interviewer was very friendly this time.

I was asked to introduce myself. Then, he directly started asking me questions 
about my project.  
 
I was asked to explain every detail and reason for usage of every technology in the 
Technology stack of the project. I had done project in web development, so I was 
asked to explain in detail about the actions that take place while linking the front 
end to the back end. He also asked me about GET, PUT and POST requests. I had 
done a project in EXTC too, so he asked me to explain detailed working of the 
same.  
 
Then he shifted to the technical questions: 
1. Arrays vs Linked lists. Why can’t binary search be performed on a linked 
list efficiently? Which sorting algorithms can be used for sorting a linked 
list? To that I answered merge sort. So, he asked me the working of merge 
sort.  
2. What are typecast operators? What happens if you assign a character to an 
integer and vice versa? I was not able to give the correct answer to this. I got 
confused whether it will give an error or not. But still I gave some relevant 
answer.  
3. What is inheritance? Applications in real world.  
 
There were other questions too but I don’t remember all of them. Then, at last he 
asked me if I had a question for him. I asked him about the role I have to play at 
SAP Labs as an intern. But before he could answer, I got disconnected due to 
connectivity issues. When I re-joined after 10 minutes, the interviewer said that its 
fine, the interview is done.  
 
After 15-20 mins, I got the mail containing the link for HR round. I was not 
expecting it because I felt that my second round was okayish. Only 4 people were 
selected for HR round.  
 
 
Interview Round 3 – (HR) 
 
The interviewer was very cheerful. The interview lasted for about 20 mins. He 
asked me to introduce myself. Then he asked a couple of questions: 
 
1. Tell me about your background. Was VJTI your first choice or did you aim 
for IITs? Do you feel sad about it? Do you regret not studying enough? 
2. Tell me about your family.  
3. What if we reject you?

4. This question was particularly tricky. He asked me as to what role I want at 
SAP Labs, to which I replied Software developer and explained why I chose 
that role. He said that at SAP, you have to be flexible for all kinds of roles. I 
sensed a red flag there and replied that I was just telling my preference, but I 
am open to any roles. (He laughed) 
5. Will you be okay with relocation for the company? 
6. What did you do in lockdown apart from studies? 
 
At last, he asked me if I had a question for him. I asked him to share his experience 
with SAP Labs so far.  
 
All 4 candidates selected for HR round got the internship offer.  
 
 
Tips:  
 
1. Start with DSA as early as possible.  
2. Solve DSA questions on Geeksforgeeks, Leetcode and Interviewbit.  
3. Be thorough with OOPS, DBMS, and OS.  
4. Take part in contests held at Codeforces and Codechef.  
5. For Dynamic Programming, refer to Aditya Verma’s playlist on Youtube.  
6. For DBMS, refer to Partha Pratim Chakraborty’s lectures on Youtube. They 
are the best lectures on DBMS so far.  
7. Be familiar with at least one language among C++ and Java. Don’t rely on 
python since for a few aptitude tests, python is not allowed.  
8. During interviews, keep yourself calm, and be confident.  
9. Don’t fake on resume since you can get caught.  
10. Explain the interviewer every detail of the code, and keep conversing. Think 
out loud and let them know your thought process. They might encourage you 
by saying that you are on right track.  
11. The most important thing: Internship doesn’t define who you are as a 
person. Don’t stress yourself too much. Don’t beat yourself up if you don’t 
get selected. There will be many more opportunities.
